As a reminder, I am planning to use the CAL FIRE Damage Inspection (DINS) dataset to answer the question: what roof type is associated with the most damage from wildfires? Previous research has illuminated the disproportionate impact of combustible roofs on structure loss rates [@collins] .

Since the DINS dataset does have information about where the fire started, I will filter these records out to do my analysis. However, I am speculating that firefighters are only able to tell where the fire started in certain cases (like when some of the structure is still standing. Therefore, I plan to also look at the full dataset and see which roof type is associated with the most damage, though I recognize there are many factors that may confound this relationship.

```{r}
#Load in libraries
library(tidyverse)
library(janitor)
library(ggplot2)
```

```{r}
#Read in data
dins = read.csv("data/raw_calfire_dins.csv")
```

```{r}
#Clean the data

# Make the column names easier to type
dins_clean <-
  clean_names(dins)

dins_select <-
  dins_clean |>
  select(
    x_damage,
    x_roof_construction,
    x_incident_name,
    if_affected_where_did_fire_start,
    latitude,
    longitude
  )

dins_select <-
  dins_select |>
  rename(
    damage = x_damage,
    roof_construction = x_roof_construction,
    incident_name = x_incident_name,
    fire_start = if_affected_where_did_fire_start
  )

```

```{r}
#Exploratory Data Analysis

head(dins_select)
tail(dins_select)
summary(dins_select)
glimpse(dins_select)
slice(dins_select)

#check if the columns are characters
is.character(dins_select$damage)

is.character(dins_select$roof_construction)

#identify what the unique values are in each column
unique(dins_select$damage)

unique(dins_select$roof_construction)

#Visualize on a graph
ggplot(dins_select, (aes(x = roof_construction))) +
  geom_bar(fill = "slategrey", color = "black") +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of Roof Types",
    x = "Roof Construction Type",
    y = "Count"
  ) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))

ggplot(dins_select, (aes(x = damage))) +
  geom_bar(fill = "firebrick", color = "black") +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of Damage Levels",
    x = "Damage Level",
    y = "Count"
  ) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1))
```

I am noting that there are quite a few empty roof types, but there is also an unknown category. So I will impute the blank ones as Unknown.

```{r}
#Impute values with na or blank as Unknown
dins_select <- dins_select |>
  mutate(roof_construction = if_else(is.na(roof_construction) | roof_construction == "" | roof_construction == " ", "Unknown", as.character(roof_construction)))

#Check if that worked
unique(dins_select$roof_construction)
```

```{r}
#Create counts table
roof_counts <- table(dins_select$roof_construction, dins_select$damage)

#turn it into a df
roof_df <- as.data.frame.matrix(roof_counts)


#compute totals for each category
roof_total <- roof_df |> 
  rownames_to_column(var = "roof_construction") |> 
  adorn_totals(where = c("row", "col"))
```

```{r}
#More EDA
head(roof_df)

tail(roof_df)

glimpse(roof_df)

#slice is irrelevant because I have so few lines

#summary doesn't mean much because it 

min(roof_df$`Destroyed (>50%)`)
max(roof_df$`Destroyed (>50%)`)
```

```{r}
#Create a subset of instances where the fire started on the roof 
dins_roof <- 
  dins_select|>
  filter(fire_start == "Roof")

#Create counts table for just fires on roof
subset_counts <- table(dins_roof$roof_construction, dins_roof$damage)

#turn it into a df
subset_df <- as.data.frame.matrix(subset_counts)


#compute totals for each category
subset_total <- subset_df |> 
  rownames_to_column(var = "roof_construction") |> 
  adorn_totals(where = c("row", "col"))
```

```{r}
#More EDA
#Visualize how many roofs of each type in the destroyed category

plot_data <- roof_total |> 
  filter(roof_construction != "Total")

ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = reorder(roof_construction, -`Destroyed (>50%)`), y = `Destroyed (>50%)`)) +
  geom_col(fill = "firebrick", color = "black") +
  labs(
    title = "Number of Destroyed Structures (>50%) by Roof Type",
    x = "Roof Construction Type",
    y = "Number of Structures Destroyed"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
```

```{r}
#Now I am just trynig out a map for fun! I will need to work on this much more...
ggplot(dins_roof, aes(x = longitude, y = latitude)) +
  geom_point(aes(color = damage, shape = roof_construction), alpha = 0.7, size = 2) +
  scale_color_brewer(palette = "Set1") + # Easy distinct color palette
  labs(
    title = "CAL FIRE DINS Structure Locations",
    subtitle = "Analysis of Damage Levels and Roof Types",
    x = "Longitude",
    y = "Latitude",
    color = "Damage Level",
    shape = "Roof Type"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

# Notes

I am very surprised to see that 87% of fire resistant roofs ended up in the \>50% destroyed category. Notably, that is for the full dataset, not just for the roof subset. When I subsetted out the houses where the fire started on the roof I am seeing that fire resistant is not present in the data. So, this could mean that houses that had fire resistant roofs had fires that started somewhere else in the building.
